mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a decline in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between RSAFS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of HOUST and UNRATE changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects diminish.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals stagflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real economic growth falters.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% quarter-over-quarter and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
